gene variants that favor men become more beneficial than those that favor women, even for women.

Genes exist in different versions or gene variants called alleles, each slightly different, and the unique set of alleles you carry (together with the environment) determines your phenotype (everything from looks to personality). Over time mutations introduce new alleles into the gene pool, where they compete for fixation.

Not only can different traits be of different importance to the sexes (maybe men could use extra bulk to compete with conspecifics, while women would benefit more by conserving the extra energy). Gene expression is not necessarily strictly additive. Genes can interact with or regulate other genes in non-additive ways. An allele can change from very beneficial to very detrimental, depending on what other alleles you carry. Men have a Y chromosome, and with it entire genes exclusive to them, that women do not carry (including the sex determining SRY gene). Because men and women do not carry the same genes, there can easily be sex differences in gene expression even for genes they do share. The same allele could therefore potentially be very beneficial to one sex, while less beneficial or even detrimental to the other sex.

Now, if an unproductive daughter has roughly as many children as a productive daughter, but an unproductive son has no children while a productive son could even have children with multiple wives, a mother carrying and selecting for alleles that more strongly favor men will have higher fitness than a mother who does not.
